source_text: Perfacile igitur studio sanctitatis, quod Deus adiuvat, potest homo carere peccatis. Si enim vincuntur peccata peccatis, quanto magis possunt virtutibus peccata superari? non vidit ingenium, quantum vos in hoc quoque iuverim, quia dixi: Aliis peccatis alia peccata vincuntur
pass_a_gloss: Perfacile therefore studio holiness, that/which God adiuvat, is-able human-being carere sins. if for vincuntur sins sins, quanto more are-able virtutibus sins superari? not vidit ingenium, quantum you in this also iuverim, because dixi: Aliis sins other sins vincuntur.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: I am amazed that such an outstanding intellect did not see how much he helped us in this too, when he said: “Some sins are overcome by other sins.”
Therefore a human being can very easily be free from sins through the pursuit of holiness, which God assists. For if sins are overcome by sins, how much more can sins be overcome by virtues?

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
